title: moe up single-command launcher
description: Objective: one command from repo root starts the whole stack. Measured at HEAD 1aa7cdc: root package.json has NO bin and no start/dev/demo script (package.json:13-32); today a user opens three terminals and hand-sets env. Components to compose (all exist, do not modify them): daemon via apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts with --dependencies=./src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts (requires MOE_STORE_PATH/MOE_PROJECT_ID/MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL trio, daemon-store-dependencies.ts:47, missing => STORE_DEPENDENCIES_ENV_MISSING); wrapper via apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts (same trio + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for claude --bare children; optional MOE_AGENT_COMMAND/MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS/MOE_WRAPPER_INTERVAL_MS/MOE_WRAPPER_ONCE, wrapper-knobs.ts:36-38). Deliverable: a launcher script (new file, e.g. scripts/moe-up.ts or bin/moe-up.ts + root package.json script entry) that validates env with named refusals BEFORE spawning, generates a dev credential + store path default when absent, starts daemon then wrapper as child processes, prints the daemon origin and control-room URL, and shuts both down cleanly on ctrl-c (Windows: rely on child.kill and Job-object semantics already used by the wrapper; external SIGTERM handlers do not fire on Windows). NOT in scope: control-room serving (separate task), packaging/CLI bin (task in Track 4), any daemon/wrapper behavior change. Verification: pnpm typecheck plus a PowerShell smoke: run the launcher with a scratch store, confirm daemon origin printed and both children exit on ctrl-c/kill without orphan processes.
definitionOfDone: One documented command (root package.json script) starts daemon + wrapper from a clean checkout with only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY preset; missing env produces a named refusal per variable before any process spawns, asserted in a test.
The launcher prints the daemon origin and exits both children cleanly on termination; a PowerShell smoke on Windows shows no orphan node processes after shutdown.
Daemon and wrapper sources are untouched; the launcher only composes existing entries via child_process with explicit argv (no shell:true).
pnpm typecheck exits 0; launcher unit tests pass with a nonzero Test Files count line; only explicit owned paths committed.
taskRails: Do not modify daemon-main.ts, agent-wrapper-main.ts, or daemon-store-dependencies.ts; compose them as-is.
Windows-first: no POSIX-only signal semantics; document the ctrl-c path and test the child-teardown path that actually runs on Windows.
No shell:true spawns; explicit argv arrays only.
TDD; refusal tests pin the exact per-variable refusal message.

implementationPlan.description: TDD the env layer first, as a PURE module. Write apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-env.test.ts RED for a resolver that takes a raw env object and returns either a complete launch config or per-variable named refusals. Behavior to pin: (a) MOE_STORE_PATH absent -> DEFAULTED to <repoRoot>/.moe-dev/store.sqlite (dev launcher, not prod), reported as defaulted; (b) MOE_PROJECT_ID absent -> defaulted to 'moe-next-dev', reported; (c) MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL absent -> a random dev credential is MINTED via crypto.randomBytes, reported as minted, never logged in full; (d) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY absent -> named refusal (the wrapper's claude --bare children cannot auth without it, per docs/agent-stack-runbook.md) unless MOE_AGENT_COMMAND is set to a non-claude command; (e) every refusal names EXACTLY the missing variable. Assert refusal identity per-variable, not just 'invalid'. No spawn, no fs writes except mkdir for the defaulted store dir (that lives in main, not here - the resolver is pure over its inputs). Two resolver runs over identical env + injected random source = identical config (determinism, injected randomness).

Shape: resolveLaunchEnv({env, repoRoot, randomHex?}) -> LaunchConfig{ok:true, agentCommand, credential, env(overlay), projectId, storePath, variables[]} | LaunchRefused{ok:false, refusals[]}. Randomness is INJECTED, defaulting to randomBytes(32).toString("hex"), which is what makes the determinism test possible without freezing the real secret. describeLaunchVariables() masks any variable flagged secret to "<minted, hidden>" so the dev credential never reaches a scrollback.

Decisions worth QA's attention:
- Empty-is-absent for all four variables, matching readStoreDependencyEnv's existing rule (daemon-store-dependencies.ts:52-57) — an exported MOE_PROJECT_ID= must not open a store under the empty project.
- isClaudeCommand() strips directory and extension before comparing, so "C:\\tools\\claude.cmd", "/usr/local/bin/claude" and "CLAUDE.EXE" all still require ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Waiving the key on a bare-name match alone would have let an absolute-path claude spawn with no auth and read as an orchestration bug.
- The refusal returns BEFORE any defaulting or minting work, so a refused launch mints no credential.

One test fixture correction during GREEN, not a production change: the store-path assertion originally compared a join()-normalized path against a forward-slash REPO_ROOT and failed on Windows (`expected false to be true` at line 41). Fixed by normalizing separators on BOTH sides before comparing; the assertion still pins the exact tail "/.moe-dev/store.sqlite" by segment rather than by re-running join(), so it is not a tautology and is platform-independent.

implementationPlan.description: Build the composer apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts + .js bridge. It spawns TWO children with EXPLICIT ARGV ARRAYS, never shell:true: (1) daemon: process.execPath + [<abs path to daemon-main.ts>, '--dependencies=<abs path to daemon-store-dependencies.ts>'] with the resolved env - NO --port flag (daemon-main.ts:44 deliberately defaults to an ephemeral port; a fixed port is how transports collide) - and read the bound origin from the daemon child's stdout log line, then print it plus the control-room hint URL; (2) wrapper: process.execPath + [<abs path to agent-wrapper-main.ts>] with the same env once the daemon origin is known. Teardown: on SIGINT AND on either child exiting, kill both children (child.kill; the wrapper's own Job-object broker reaps its claude grandchildren on Windows) and exit with the first failure's code. Cross-platform note IN CODE: external SIGTERM does not reach Node handlers on Windows - the reliable teardown trigger is child-exit cascade + Ctrl-C on the console. TDD: a test drives the composer with MOE_AGENT_COMMAND pointed at a tiny node script standing in for both children (fast, no real daemon), asserting spawn argv shapes, origin parsing, and both-children teardown on one child's death. Do NOT modify daemon-main.ts, agent-wrapper-main.ts, or daemon-store-dependencies.ts.

Composer behavior:
- Refuses BEFORE spawning: on a refusal it logs each refusal.message and returns 1 with zero spawn calls (asserted: harness.calls toHaveLength 0). A launcher that spawns first and refuses second leaves a half-started stack.
- Daemon argv: process.execPath + [<abs daemon-main.ts>, "--dependencies=<abs daemon-store-dependencies.ts>"], argv length pinned to exactly 2 and `argv.filter(startsWith("--port"))` pinned to [] — that pair is what makes drill (iii) redden, protecting daemon-main.ts:48-54's deliberate ephemeral bind.
- Origin: parsed from an ACCUMULATED stdout buffer, not per chunk (a pipe can split "listening on <origin>" anywhere; a chunk-only match would hang). Regex pinned to daemon-entry.ts:228's wording, so a peer changing that line reddens THIS suite rather than only the smoke.
- Wrapper starts only AFTER the origin: asserted by spawn count 1 before the line and 2 after, argv length exactly 1.
- Control-room hint names MOE_DAEMON_ORIGIN — verified as the real override apps/control-room/vite.config.ts:22 reads (`process.env["MOE_DAEMON_ORIGIN"] ?? "http://127.0.0.1:39123"`), not an invented variable.
- Teardown: one latch. Either child exiting, or Ctrl-C, kills both. Double Ctrl-C asserted to leave killCount exactly 1 per child. Exit code is the first nonzero child code (daemon exits 3 -> runMoeUp returns 3), else 0.
- Two DISTINCT named refusals where the plan asked for one: MOE_UP_DAEMON_EXITED_BEFORE_LISTENING (a child exited) vs MOE_UP_DAEMON_ORIGIN_TIMEOUT (silent daemon, killed rather than hung). Discriminated by fleet.childExited(), each asserted by its own code.
- Windows note is IN CODE at the module header: external SIGTERM never reaches a Node handler on Windows; the two triggers that do fire are console Ctrl-C and child exit, and killing the wrapper reaps its claude grandchildren through the wrapper's own Job-object broker.

Test-honesty notes: FakeChild.kill() schedules a real exit, so a launcher that killed but never awaited its children would hang instead of reading green. Beyond the fake-spawn unit tests there is a REAL end-to-end test using the production createProcessSpawn() against stub entry scripts under a temp dir whose path CONTAINS A SPACE ("moe up real-…") — it proves the shipped spawn adapter works with no shell:true and correct argv quoting, so the injected-port tests are not the only evidence.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW found THREE real defects in my own diff, all on error paths, all fixed with tests written RED first (both RED runs reproduced the exact raw crash predicted: "Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, mkdir ..." and "Error: EAGAIN: could not fork").
1. ORPHANED DAEMON. If the wrapper's spawn threw (EAGAIN, exhausted process table, bad interpreter) the exception escaped runMoeUp while the daemon was ALREADY RUNNING — leaving exactly the orphan the whole teardown cascade exists to prevent. Now caught: logs MOE_UP_WRAPPER_START_FAILED, calls stopEverything, awaits the daemon's exit, returns nonzero. Test asserts the daemon child's killCount is 1 and no second child was created.
2. A CRASH IS NOT A REFUSAL. An unwritable dev store directory threw a raw ENOTDIR stack out of a launcher that had spawned nothing. Now returns 1 with MOE_UP_STORE_DIR_UNWRITABLE and zero spawns, asserted.
3. UNBOUNDED BUFFER. The stdout accumulator used for origin parsing kept appending for the entire life of the launcher — a daemon logging for days would grow that string forever. The buffer is now released the moment the origin lands (`seen = null`, watcher short-circuits). Fixed but NOT tested: the leak has no observable behavior, and a test that cannot see it would be theater. Flagging it for QA rather than claiming coverage.

Considered and deliberately NOT changed: two concurrent `moe up` runs share the default .moe-dev store and would each mint a different operator credential against it. Real but out of scope for a dev launcher, and the operator's escape hatch is setting MOE_STORE_PATH — noted rather than locked.
